To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
OFDMA networks can be efficiently exploited by multimedia flows, if the application layer is able to adapt to the available bandwidth, which can be dynamically changed by the MAC layer.

the soft capacity of OFDMA can support a large number of users, provided that they are able to exploit the available capacity in a flexible manner, by adapting their traffic to the available network capacity, rather than trying to maintain a constant rate.
OFDMA networks are suitable for soft capacity, and that soft capacity is suitable for soft multimedia traffic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the soft QoS of OFDMA networks, and with the investigation of the impact on network resources of soft QoS multimedia content.
the design of an efficient and scalable medium access control protocol for next generation wireless networks.
the design of a novel medium access control scheme for multimedia traffic, which exploits the soft QoS nature of the traffic and the soft capacity of the network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soft capacity is indeed a viable option for multimedia traffic, but a careful design is needed on the application and network sides, to fully exploit this potential.

the soft QoS paradigm, which is a natural fit for multimedia applications, can be effectively exploited in next generation wireless access networks, but it is up to the applications to fully benefit from the potential of the soft QoS approach.
the soft capacity concept can be successfully applied to OFDMA-based next generation networks, provided that the application layer is able to properly adapt to the network conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if multimedia users adapt to the available resources, they can be supported by a soft capacity network.
the OFDMA MAC protocol, in its current form, is suitable for soft multimedia traffic, but it requires a careful design and implementation of the application layer to fully take advantage of it.
the soft capacity of OFDMA is a good match for soft QoS of multimedia traffic, provided that the latter is properly managed on the application side.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by properly managing soft capacity, multimedia traffic can be efficiently carried in next generation wireless systems.
, if properly designed, next generation wireless networks will be able to support multimedia traffic with soft QoS requirements, and that this can be achieved with a very limited overhead.

, if properly exploited, soft QoS multimedia applications can take advantage of the flexibility and softness of the underlying network, thus providing a very good tradeoff between network resources and user experience.
